tests.name: Quick Check
tests.description: Timed check on Verse Literature Exam Technique

questions.question: Q: What does PEA stand for and why is it important?
questions.correctAnswer: Point, Evidence, Analysis. Make a point about a feature, quote the Latin as evidence, and analyse the effect. This ensures every analytical claim is supported by textual evidence.

questions.question: Q: List six poetic features you should be prepared to discuss.
questions.correctAnswer: Alliteration, enjambement, elision, caesura, onomatopoeia, hyperbaton, simile, metaphor, word order, assonance (any six).

questions.question: Q: How should you structure a 10-mark evaluation question?
questions.correctAnswer: Introduction stating your thesis, 3-4 paragraphs each with PEA (point supported by Latin quotation and analysis), and a brief conclusion.

tests.name: Exam-Style Practice
tests.description: Short-answer practice on Verse Literature Exam Technique

questions.question: Q: What should you discuss when asked about a character in a set text?
questions.correctAnswer: How the author presents them: through their own words and actions, through other characters' reactions, through the narrator's commentary, and why the author portrays them this way.

questions.question: Q: How do you approach a comparison question?
questions.correctAnswer: Identify both similarities and differences. Use comparative connectives. Support each comparison with Latin quotations from both passages.

questions.question: Q: What is the time management rule for the literature exam?
questions.correctAnswer: Roughly 1 minute per mark. A 10-mark question deserves about 10 minutes.

questions.question: Q: What should you avoid when translating verse?
questions.correctAnswer: Avoid overly literal translations that sound unnatural in English, AND overly free translations that lose the Latin's precise meaning. Aim for accurate, idiomatic English.

questions.question: Q: How do you discuss metre in an exam answer?
questions.correctAnswer: Identify the metre (e.g. dactylic hexameter for epic), and explain how the rhythm contributes to meaning.
